S1.l1: A q-contraction on a complete metric space has a unique fixed point x^* (Banach).

S2.l2: Write x_{n+1}-x^*=(1-h_n)(x_n-x^*)+h_n(f(x_n)-f(x^*)) and use the contraction bound on the second term.

S4.l1: Key lemma. If each block of m steps has h-sum at least \delta, the product over a block is at most e^{-(1-q)\delta}.
S4.l2:
Apply S3 inside each block with a_n=h_n(1-q). The blocks multiply, so the product over k blocks is at most e^{-k(1-q)\delta}.

Individual steps may vanish; only the block sums matter.
S4.l3:
\prod_{n\in B}(1-h_n(1-q))\le\exp\Bigl(-(1-q)\sum_{n\in B}h_n\Bigr)\le e^{-(1-q)\delta}

Steps before the first full block contribute a factor at most 1.

S5.l1: By S2 the error is bounded by the product of factors; S4 sends that product to 0.
S5.l2: Iterate S2 from index 0; group the factors into blocks and apply S4.

S6.l1: With h_n=1/n the sum diverges like \log n, so S3 gives a polynomial rate.
